newsitem.title: UK: BA overhauls Deutsche BA on routes, managers.
newsitem.headline: BA overhauls Deutsche BA on routes, managers.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Thursday it would overhaul its German unit Deutsche BA, cutting three international routes but expanding the domestic service.
It said there would also be a number of management changes, with Richard Heideker stepping down at his own request from the role of managing director on October 31.
BA said its German alliance would launch services from early next year from its Munich base to Hamburg and Cologne, with eight flights a day to each destination.
Frequencies will increase on all of its existing five domestic routes from March 1997, the airline said.
But flights on three loss-making international routes -- Munich to Paris, Munich to Madrid and Berlin to Oslo -- will be cut, BA added in a statement.
Deutsche BA plans to withdraw all its Fokker 100s and focus entirely on Boeing 737s by autumn 1997, which will result in "significant cost savings and opertional efficiencies."
BA said Deutsche BA would also shortly announce significant changes to its service, emphasising improved schedules and punctuality, to be introduced next year.
Heideker's departure will be at the end of January 1997, after shareholders asked him to stay on for three months to assist with the sale of the turboprop operation, announced earlier this month.

Paul Giblin will become Deutsche BA's commercial director from his current post as area manager for Germany, while Adrian Hunt will become operations director, from his position as commercial director for BA Engineering in London.
Wolfgang Grund, currently managing director of Deutsche BA Holdings, will become managing director of Deutsche BA on November 1.
"It was a pleasure to work with (Heideker) and I wish him every success in the future," said BA's managing director Bob Ayling.

Deutsche BA had turnover of 492 million marks in the year to March 31, 1996 and carried 2.2 million passengers, BA said, with turnover of 272 million marks in the first half of the current year as 1.2 million passengers were carried. September was a record month, BA said, with 233,000 passengers carried.

BA routinely declines to detail chronic losses at Deutsche BA and its French subsidiary TAT but said combined losses from DBA and TAT together fell to 68 million stg in the year to March 31 1996, down from a 93 million stg deficit in 1994/1995.
Analysts estimate about two-thirds of those losses were attributable to TAT.
Earlier this week BA offered 25 million French francs to buy insolvent French airline Air Liberte, saying it could make the company profitable by running it in tandem with TAT.
Other bidders for Air Liberte include a French consortium, while Richard Branson's Virgin airline has also expressed an interest.
